Compa SA Posts Stable First-Quarter Results Amid Steady Automotive Demand

Romanian automotive component manufacturer Compa SA reported stable first-quarter results on Wednesday, buoyed by resilient demand in the European automotive sector and ongoing efficiency efforts. 

The Sibiu-based company posted revenues of RON 248 million for the three months ended March 31, up 3.7% from RON 239 million in the same period last year. Net profit reached RON 13.2 million, marking a slight increase of 2.5% compared to the previous year’s first quarter.

“We are pleased to report a solid start to the year, reflecting our diversified client base and ongoing process improvements,” said Mircea Popa, Chief Executive Officer of Compa SA, in a statement accompanying the results. “Our order book remains strong, and we are committed to further enhancing operational efficiency in the coming quarters.”

The company, a prominent supplier of components such as turbocharger parts, axle assemblies, and gear housings, cited steady production volumes at its Sibiu facility. Export sales accounted for 68% of total revenues, benefiting from robust demand in Western European markets.

Analysts noted that Compa SA’s performance reflects broader stability in the regional automotive supply chain. “Compa’s results are in line with moderate industry growth across Central and Eastern Europe,” said Andrei Ionescu, an analyst at Carpathian Capital. “No major disruptions or shocks have impacted production or deliveries this quarter.”

Romania’s automotive sector, a key pillar of the national economy, continues to attract investment amid a push for greater localization of supply chains. Compa SA reiterated its full-year guidance and said it would continue investing in automation and workforce training throughout 2024.
